claims.explanation: Vemurafenib selectively kills cancer lines that depend on BRAF-driven MAPK signaling, primarily those harboring activating BRAF mutations (especially V600E), while lines lacking BRAF mutations or with alternative MAPK activation (e.g., KRAS/NRAS mutations, EGFR feedback) are less affected. The pattern is consistent with oncogene addiction to mutant BRAF, and resistance in BRAF-mutant colorectal lines is explained by EGFR-mediated feedback reactivation.

features.basis: Activating BRAF mutations, especially V600E, predict response to vemurafenib in melanoma and other cancers.
EGFR feedback activation mediates resistance to BRAF inhibition in BRAF-mutant colorectal cancer.
NF1 loss causes resistance to vemurafenib in melanoma models.
MED12 loss confers resistance to vemurafenib in CRISPR screens.
KRAS mutations activate MAPK signaling downstream of BRAF, reducing dependence on BRAF.
NRAS mutations activate MAPK pathway and are associated with poor response to BRAF inhibitors.
PTEN loss co-occurs with BRAF mutations in sensitive melanoma lines, though mechanism unclear.
CUL3 loss identified as a resistance factor in CRISPR screen.
TADA2B loss identified as a resistance factor in CRISPR screen.
TADA1 loss identified as a resistance factor in CRISPR screen.
NF2 loss identified as a resistance factor in CRISPR screen.
